samples.claim: MemWalIndexDetails centralizes configuration, base compaction progress, and shard snapshots. Writers read configuration; snapshots are point-in-time optimizations, while readers requiring current shards list directories and latest shard manifests. Background refresh does not make snapshots authoritative mutable shard state. Snapshot Lance-file schema lists shard_id utf8, shard_spec_id uint32, typed shard_field_{id}. snapshot_ts_millis int64=1 and num_shards uint32=2 describe it; optional inline_snapshots bytes=3 holds Lance bytes for small counts. The threshold example 100 is explicitly implementation-defined, not a specified constant.

samples.claim: The returned mapped JoinHandle produces the original closure Result on a successful join. For JoinError, try_into_panic recovers and resume_unwind rethrows the original panic payload; non-panic join errors trigger a new explanatory panic. The closure may outlive the returned handle; this wrapper contains no explicit cancellation/abort API or cancellation token. Exact Tokio detach/shutdown semantics belong to the dependency and are not reconstructed here. Span entry is scoped to closure execution.
samples.evidence:
194 |     // arrives as a `JoinError` still carrying its payload, so resuming it
195 |     // re-raises the original panic in the caller. Reporting the closure's
196 |     // outcome over a channel instead loses that -- the sender drops unsent and
197 |     // every panic in any `spawn_cpu` closure surfaces identically as an opaque
198 |     // `RecvError`, pointing here rather than at the fault.
199 |     handle.map(|res| match res {
200 |         Ok(result) => result,
201 |         Err(join_error) => match join_error.try_into_panic() {
202 |             Ok(panic) => std::panic::resume_unwind(panic),
203 |             // The CPU runtime outlives every caller, so its tasks are not
204 |             // cancelled out from under one.
205 |             Err(join_error) => panic!("spawn_cpu task failed: {join_error}"),
206 |         },
207 |     })
208 | }

samples.claim: Builder option methods use with_, APIs prefer Into/AsRef, internals prefer pub(crate), public re-exports define the surface, and enums/typed structs replace magic numbers/unstructured maps. Keep physical RowAddr and stable RowId distinct; use RowAddress helpers and Roaring/RowAddrTreeMap selections. User counts subtract deletions; traits stay minimal; schema introspection must not materialize rows. Persistent formats are stable/versioned; Arrow access uses typed accessors (optional variants unless type proven); local IO writes use single syscalls instead of cloud multipart machinery.
samples.evidence:
24 | ## API Design
25 | 
26 | - Use `with_`-prefixed builder methods for optional config (e.g., `MyStruct::new(required).with_option(v)`) — don't create separate constructor variants.
27 | - For public APIs, prefer `Into<T>` or `AsRef<T>` trait bounds for flexible inputs.
28 | - Prefer `pub(crate)` over `pub` for crate-internal items. Use `pub use` re-exports for the actual public API surface.
29 | - Use enums instead of magic numbers for format versions, variant types, and discriminators — leverage exhaustive `match`.
30 | - Use strongly-typed structs instead of `HashMap<String, String>` in APIs — convert to strings only at serialization boundaries.
31 | - Keep `RowAddr` (physical fragment+offset) and `RowId` (stable logical identifier) as distinct types — never raw `u64` for both.
32 | - Use `RowAddress` from `lance-core/src/utils/address.rs` instead of raw bitwise operations on row addresses.
33 | - Use `RowAddrTreeMap`/`RoaringBitmap` instead of `Vec<Range<u64>>` for physical row selections.
34 | - Use logical row counts (`num_rows()`) instead of `physical_rows` for user-facing metrics — subtract deletions.
35 | - Keep traits minimal — only core abstraction methods. Move helpers to standalone functions and config to struct fields.
36 | - Get column/field types from schema metadata — never materialize data rows just to inspect types.
37 | - Use stable, versioned serialization formats for persistent storage (e.g., index files) — avoid unstable cross-version formats.
38 | - Use Arrow's type-safe access (`ArrayAccessor` trait bounds, `as_*_array` helpers) instead of `arrow::compute::cast` + `downcast_ref`. Prefer `_opt` variants (e.g., `as_string_opt`) unless the data type has already been verified.
39 | - In `lance-io/`, use single-syscall writes for local filesystem I/O — don't reuse cloud multipart upload machinery.
40 |
samples.review_note: Matches Rust API guide requirements as policy.
